q: You are optimizing a high-concurrency web server and notice memory usage spikes when multiple clients request massive video assets simultaneously. How should you fix this bottleneck?
options: Read the asset files into memory using fs.readFileSync
Stream the assets incrementally using fs.createReadStream
Allocate large temporary storage spaces using Buffer.alloc
Fork separate child processes for every incoming media connection
explain: Using fs.createReadStream streams files in small, sequential chunks. This avoids loading entire large files into RAM all at once and keeps memory usage stable.

q: You are building a real-time analytics hub and want to define and trigger custom application events across separate asynchronous modules. Which native class handles this?
explain: The EventEmitter class from the events module allows you to implement custom pub/sub patterns by binding callback handlers to distinct event names.

q: You are integrating an enterprise REST API where routing requirements, validation, and request pipelines are growing too fast for a raw http module server. What framework should you adopt?
explain: Express abstracts raw HTTP server implementations into an organized, middleware-driven framework that simplifies routing, header parsing, and request handling.

q: You are writing a pipeline script that parses a log file and must instantly stop future reads if a specific error message appears in a chunk. What stream method halts execution?
explain: The stream.destroy() method immediately closes the underlying stream and frees resource descriptors, preventing any further data chunks from being emitted.

q: You are refactoring a deeply nested chain of asynchronous callbacks that has become unreadable and hard to maintain. Which approach cleans up this callback hell without external libraries?
options: Convert your asynchronous code blocks to use async/await
Isolate variables using the global process context
Batch asynchronous operations using synchronous nextTick utilities
Split your business logic into separate EventEmitter instances
explain: Refactoring asynchronous operations to use Promises with async/await replaces nested callbacks with clean, linear code that reads like synchronous logic.

q: You are developing a secure authentication service and want to separate your network server logic from your main Express application router setup. Why is this separation beneficial?
options: It allows you to test route logic without making actual network calls
It guarantees complete thread isolation within the V8 engine
It prevents cross-site scripting vulnerabilities in template engines
It bypasses the single-threaded event loop architecture entirely
explain: Separating your Express app from the network server setup allows you to pass the app instance to testing utilities, executing functional tests in-process without spinning up TCP ports.

q: You are writing an authentication guard that needs to execute validation logic, update headers, and conditionally halt incoming HTTP requests before they reach your final endpoints. What should you write?
options: An asynchronous event listener on process
A child process worker thread script
explain: Express middleware functions have access to the request, response, and the next middleware in line. They can execute code, modify payloads, or end requests early.

q: You need to allocate a raw binary storage buffer of a fixed size, ensuring that any residual data in memory is completely wiped before use. Which constructor method is safe?
explain: Buffer.alloc(size) initializes a new buffer of the specified size and fills it with zeros, which prevents sensitive leftover data from leaking out of raw memory.

q: An interactive command-line interface tool built on Node.js crashes with an uncaught error. You want to intercept this crash globally to log diagnostic details before exiting. What listener handles this?
explain: The uncaughtException event on the process object intercepts errors that slip through try/catch blocks, giving you a chance to log system diagnostics before shutting down.

q: You want to scale a real-time web application to utilize all 8 CPU cores on a host server, allowing worker instances to share the same inbound port. Which built-in module solves this?
explain: The cluster module spawns worker processes that share a master server port, using internal routing logic to automatically distribute incoming network load.

q: You are writing an automated deployment tool that needs to trigger an external shell command and buffer its complete text output in memory upon termination. Which method is most appropriate?
explain: The child_process.exec method runs a command within an operating system shell and buffers its entire stdout/stderr output before passing it to a callback function upon completion.

q: You are processing large batches of structured log entries and need to modify the data payload format on the fly as it moves from a read stream to a write stream. What type of stream do you need?
explain: A Transform stream is a specialized Duplex stream that takes input chunks, applies custom modifications, and passes the updated results to an attached downstream target.

q: You need to create a secure hashing routine for user passwords using standard OpenSSL implementations. Which native core module provides this functionality?
explain: The crypto module provides cryptographic tools that wrap OpenSSL functionalities like hmac, sign, cipher, and secure hashing algorithms.

q: You need to build a raw TCP chat server that manages persistent sockets and handles incoming binary text frames cleanly. Which native core module provides these networking tools?
explain: The net core module provides an asynchronous network API to construct stream-based TCP or IPC connections, making it ideal for building raw socket utilities.

q: Your file processing script uses an asynchronous loop. You need to verify internal file metrics and throw immediate assertions if data validations fail. Which core validation module should you use?
explain: The assert module provides assertion testing functions that evaluate expression assumptions, throwing errors if invariants are violated.

q: You are writing a service utility and need to inspect the current environment paths to distinguish if your script is executing on a Windows platform or a Unix environment. Which property tells you this?
explain: The process.platform string returns a tag identifier identifying the host OS environment, such as 'darwin', 'freebsd', 'linux', or 'win32'.

q: You are integrating an asynchronous job control tracking array. You need to structure a worker queue that accepts a concurrency constraint integer along with a task handler. Which package provides this?
explain: The async control flow library provides utility functions like async.queue to build asynchronous task queues with strict concurrency limits.

q: You are developing a background file watcher and want to defer an execution step so that it runs right after active I/O polling operations conclude, without starving the event loop. What should you use?
explain: The setImmediate timer queues callbacks to run during the check phase of the event loop, immediately after I/O polling completes. This prevents I/O starvation.

q: You have a single-threaded server script that executes a heavy data operation, blocking all incoming API requests for 5 seconds. What is the best classification for this operation?
explain: CPU-bound calculations execute synchronously on Node's main thread. This stalls the single-threaded event loop and blocks incoming network I/O operations until the task completes.

q: You want to read input straight from a terminal prompt, process it as a JavaScript command statement, and print the results back to the screen in a continuous loop. What environment does this describe?
options: An unbuffered cryptography hash verify loop
explain: A REPL (Read-Eval-Print Loop) environment accepts user inputs, evaluates expressions, prints the computed results, and loops until explicitly closed.

q: You are creating a command-line script and need to intercept a termination event like Ctrl+C to run cleanups before exiting. Which signal event listener should you register?
explain: The SIGINT signal is sent by terminal environments when a user interrupts a process with Ctrl+C. Listening for this allows you to run cleanups before exiting.

q: You are writing a system installation script and need to retrieve the home directory path of the active user across different target operating systems. Which utility function resolves this?
explain: The os.homedir() method looks up environmental settings to return the absolute path to the active user's home directory across both Unix and Windows systems.

q: Your team is running a high-throughput video streaming service. They want to ensure data chunks are pushed to users immediately without being accumulated in internal framework buffers. What feature represents this?
explain: Node's streaming architecture processes data chunks sequentially as they arrive. This avoids buffering delays and ensures fast delivery to downstream clients.

q: You are building a custom monitoring tool and want to trace the life cycle of asynchronous operations across network requests. Which experimental core module exposes hooks for this?
explain: The async_hooks core module provides an API to track the lifetime of asynchronous resources created within your application.

q: You want to implement custom routing logic within a basic HTTP server, inspecting inbound path segments natively without using third-party frameworks. Which strategy do you execute?
options: Evaluate the req.url parameter within createServer
Inject custom actions using the cluster module
Map distinct ports to separate asset utilities
Register individual listeners on EventEmitter targets
explain: The req.url property provides the incoming request path string. You can parse this string inside your createServer callback to implement basic routing rules.
